govdocs-archive_org-PaulRassinierCollect: Rassinier’s book bangs the drum for the deniers’ tale. The Frenchman’s sayings find no friends among bookmen. Set it by the true histories. The proofs against it pile mountain-high. The book fits the lie-shelf; read it with both eyes open.
tecumseh-a-drama: Canadian poet Charles Mair dramatizes the life of Tecumseh, the Shawnee chief who dreamed of a united Indigenous nation. Written in blank verse, the play honors its hero's nobility and tragic fate. A landmark of Canadian literature and a tribute to a great Native leader.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alabama: A 1913 entry on Alabama — the state's Catholic story, centered on Mobile. Thomas Owen traces its growth. French settlers brought the faith early. The missions spread with the frontier. A southern Church, steadily built. Its cathedral honors the Immaculate Conception. Its missions date to the French colonial days.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alma: This 1913 reference article on alma — the Hebrew word for maiden. Romain Butin weighs its famous use. Isaiah's prophecy turns on its sense. Virgin or young woman, scholars debate. A single word of vast import. Its translation shaped the Christmas story.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ama: This 1913 reference article on ama — the biblical handmaid's title. Maurice Hassett explains its humble sense. The word veils lowly service. Scripture's maids bear it with honor. A small word of the old law. Its modesty suits the Gospel maids. Its use is rare but reverent.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anathema: This 1913 reference piece on anathema — the Church's solemn curse. Joseph Gignac explains its terrible weight. Let him be cut off, the councils cried. The Church wields it sparingly. The heaviest word in canon law. Its bell, book, and candle awed sinners.
